title: After-call presentation replacement rewrites terminal evidence outcome
claim: When Tool::execute returns Ok(ToolResult) and an after-tool hook changes is_error, the runtime records ToolExecutionOutcome from the replacement presentation result rather than from the actual tool result.

evidence.detail: The fixed authorization chain classifies after_tool_call replacement as a presentation transform after Tool::execute.
The actual Ok(result) is cloned into the hook and then replaced by final_result.
ExecutedTool::ordinary derives Succeeded or Failed solely from the supplied result.is_error.
The supplied result is final_result, so the presentation replacement determines the outcome field.
complete_tool_call emits that derived outcome as terminal tool evidence.
The existing replacement test proves later authority stability but never captures or asserts the tool outcome evidence, so it does not refute the claim.

reproduction: Concrete case: a tool returns Ok(ToolResult { is_error: false, ... }); after_tool_call returns Replace(ToolResult { is_error: true, ... }); the emitted ToolExecutionOutcome is Failed although Tool::execute succeeded.

title: Current audit head has no three-platform acceptance result
claim: The exact committed audit baseline has no Linux/macOS/Windows Phase 17 acceptance result, so platform identity and passage cannot be established for the current implementation.

evidence.detail: The committed workflow defines a three-platform Phase 17 matrix, which proves selection but not execution or passage.
gh run list returned an empty array and the checks API returned HTTP 422 because this exact local commit is not present on the remote.
The current baseline contains substantial post-exit Phase 17 runtime and test changes, so the historical matrix recorded by the Phase ledger cannot establish the current baseline.
All focused Phase 17 suites passed on Windows, but no current Linux or macOS execution evidence exists.
